request: Set the camera so that the white surface uses most of the camera's range without saturating, and report the exposure and gain you chose.

dialogue.content: Set the camera so that the white surface uses most of the camera's range without saturating, and report the exposure and gain you chose.

Decision 1/10 -> hardware
Instruction: Aim the camera at the white surface. Set gain to the minimum (lowest noise) and start with a moderate exposure. Grab a frame, and read the max pixel value and the fraction of saturated pixels (also the mean and a high percentile, e.g. 99.9%). Adjust exposure iteratively (scale it by target/peak, using a target of about 85-90% of full scale, e.g. ~215-230 of 255 for 8-bit) until the peak is high and no pixels are saturated. Raise gain only if the maximum exposure is not enough. Check the frame again at the final settings. Report the final exposure (with units), the gain, the bit depth, and the measured peak, mean, and saturated fraction. Return only values the camera reported.
Reason: The camera must be driven to find and verify exposure and gain on the white surface.
